reductionFrom.formalDefinition: SAT = {Φ | Φ is a satisfiable Boolean formula}
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: SAT, or the Boolean satisfiability problem, is a problem that asks for a list of assignments to the literals of phi to result in 'True'
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether Φ is satisfiable
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Boolean formula. Clauses joined by '&', literals within a clause joined by '|', negation prefix '!' written directly before the name. Variable names start with a letter or '_' and contain only letters, digits and '_'. When there are several clauses, each clause with more than one literal must be in parentheses. Each clause has 1+ literals of any size. Example: (x1 | !x2 | x3) & (!x1 | x2)
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Comma-separated variable:value pairs, optionally wrapped in parentheses. Booleans must be capitalized True/False (T/F also accepted); ':' or '=' may be used as the separator. List every variable you are assigning. Example: (x1:True,x2:False,x3:True)

reductionTo.formalDefinition: 3SAT = {Φ | Φ is a satisfiable Boolean formula in 3CNF}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: 3SAT is the Boolean satisfiability problem restricted to formulas in conjunctive normal form with at most three literals per clause. It asks whether there is an assignment of True/False values to the variables of Φ that makes the whole formula True.
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether Φ is satisfiable
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Boolean formula in 3-CNF. Clauses joined by '&', literals within a clause joined by '|', negation prefix '!' written directly before the name. Variable names start with a letter or '_' and contain only letters, digits and '_'. When there are several clauses, each clause with more than one literal must be in parentheses. Each clause has at most 3 literals. Example: (x1 | !x2 | x3) & (!x1 | x3 | x1)
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Comma-separated variable:Boolean pairs, optionally wrapped in parentheses. Booleans must be capitalized True/False (T/F also accepted); ':' or '=' may be used as the separator. List every variable you are assigning. Example: (x1:True,x2:False,x3:True)

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a O(2^n) solution algorithm for the 3SAT problem which implements a back tracking algorithm to find an exact assignment boolean assignment of variables to satisfy the problem instance.
